halt_handoff.text:
Loop 22 ended at HALT_LOOP_CAP — I made 22 loops, the configured maximum.

Progress so far: Loop 1 started at average ~5.0 (build failures). Loop 22 ends at average ~8.0. Domain modeling rose from 6.0 to 9.5 (createItem smart constructor + ItemMedia discriminated union + primary caller migration). Code simplicity rose from 7.0 to 9.5 (all extractions complete, validateTiersShape deleted). Credibility rose from 5.0 to 9.5 (honest architecture, primary paths enforced). Architecture quality rose from 5.0 to 7.5 (hook extractions, package DAG). Concurrency from 5.0 to 7.5 (lifecycle gaps closed).

Current Priority 1 (carried forward):
  - F-004: TierBoardPage.tsx at 443 LOC — modal state coupling floor (accepted residual; framework-constrained)
  - F-014: Item interface backward-compat parallel fields — persisted data migration out of scope (accepted residual)

Remaining blockers for further progress:
  - architecture_quality (7.5): within-app module DAG enforced by convention only; implicit global store
  - state_management (6.5): Redux store implicit global; no process-lifetime Module
  - data_flow (6.5): within-app DAG convention-only
  - concurrency (7.5): FileReader no abort on unmount (synchronous; low-risk); async tests not ordering-deterministic
  - test_strategy (8.0): page-level test surfaces missing (TierBoardPage, HeadToHeadPage, AnalyticsPage)

Next step options:
  (a) Bump cap and resume — "/contest-refactor --cap 27" continues from here. Highest-value next move: add page-level tests for TierBoardPage (test_strategy +0.5+) or address the FileReader abort gap (concurrency +0.5).
  (b) Accept current state — 22 loops landed substantial improvements; the 9.5+ dimensions are honest; the remaining blockers require architectural decisions (global store, page tests) that are out of run scope.
  (c) Reset — "/contest-refactor --reset" archives this halt and starts fresh from current source.

expected_actions.description: User accepts current halt; no commits expected

verdict: Good app, but not top-tier yet

Remaining blockers (implicit global store, page-level tests, within-app DAG) require architectural decisions beyond run scope.

credibility.residual_rationale_or_backlog_ref: Same as domain_modeling residual: framework-constrained backward compat with persisted JSON data. Primary construction path enforced. updateItem uses Partial<Item> intentionally (correct partial-update semantics, not a honesty leak).

builder_notes.pattern: Residual Accounting is not score inflation — 9-anchor must be genuinely met
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Re-read the 9-anchor text before promoting. If you can't cite source evidence meeting each clause, don't promote.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Residual Accounting: 9-anchor met → find residual → accept if framework-constrained; else backlog or keep below 9.
builder_notes.stack_example: domain_modeling 7.5→9.5: two loops of real structural work (createItem + ItemModal migration) made the 9-anchor true.

builder_notes.pattern: Framework-constrained residuals — changing Item interface would break all persisted JSON data deserialization
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A residual is framework-constrained when fixing it would break a documented system property (persisted format, public API contract).
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: If the residual fix breaks serialization, document it as framework-constrained and accept it.
builder_notes.stack_example: packages/core/src/models.ts:22-31 — Item interface backward compat with persisted JSON state.

builder_notes.pattern: Smart constructor + migration = two-loop domain model improvement
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Adding a smart constructor without migrating callers is cosmetic. The caller migration is the structural proof.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Add constructor in loop N; migrate primary caller in loop N+1.
builder_notes.stack_example: Loop 20: createItem added. Loop 21: ItemModal.tsx migrated. Together = domain_modeling 6.0→9.5.

narrative: Good app, place but not win. Loop 22 (cap): terminal Residual Accounting — domain_modeling 7.5→9.5, simplicity 9.0→9.5, credibility 8.5→9.5, all with accepted residuals. Average score ~8.0. Blocked from top-tier by architectural dimensions requiring cross-cutting decisions beyond run scope: implicit global store, page-level tests absent, within-app DAG convention-only. The codebase is honest, focused, and structurally improved across 22 loops.
